players.product: data center buildings owned and operated for GPU clusters (owner / operator of the Columbus, Georgia site hosting Axe Compute's B300 cluster)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Adrian Goldfarb: total revenue from continuing operations (now excluding the divested rail business) for Q2 2026 increased 30% to $6.18 million from $4.77 million; Technology Solutions contributed $3.23 million, 'our largest revenue line against a zero year ago', and related party services and consulting revenue was $2.91 million, including $2.71 million of one-time accelerated recognition of the remaining APR deferred revenue; first-half revenue was $8.32 million versus $8.68 million. Gross margin was $3.45 million or 55.8% of revenue (37.3% a year ago); operating expenses $3.4 million; income from operations approximately $50,000 versus a $1.54 million loss. Including a one-time gain on the sale of investments, net income from continuing operations was $48.7 million (basic EPS $1.61, diluted $1.37) and consolidated net income $47.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA (excluding that gain and stock-based compensation) was positive at approximately $0.5 million - 'we got there ahead of plan'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $6.18 million (+30%); gross margin 55.8%; adjusted EBITDA approximately $0.5 million; EPS $1.61 basic / $1.37 diluted

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Adrian Goldfarb ('We guide to what is contracted, deposited, and scheduled, not to what is possible'): bookings at the end of Q2 represented approximately $43.5 million of revenue expected to be recognized in 2026, plus approximately $1.1 million of 2025 Technology Solutions deferred revenue; Duos reconfirmed 2026 total revenue to exceed $50 million - approximately $26 million from GPU-as-a-Service as the deployment comes online in the second half and approximately $25 million from the Technology Solutions backlog. Adjusted EBITDA is expected positive in the third and fourth quarters, with fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA of $8 million to $10 million; fourth-quarter recurring infrastructure revenue (GPU-as-a-Service, colocation and hosting) of approximately $17 million to $18 million, an annualized recurring revenue exit run rate in excess of $70 million under multiyear agreements at gross margins well above 70%. The early 2027 framework calls for total revenues of at least $160 million from announced and contracted programs only, with formal 2027 guidance at Q3 results; the first-half cost increase was onetime, and headcount fell from about 100 to about 25 full-time people.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue to exceed $50 million (GPU-as-a-Service approximately $26 million, Technology Solutions approximately $25 million); Q4 adjusted EBITDA $8 million to $10 million; ARR exit run rate in excess of $70 million; 2027 revenue at least $160 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker: the Technology Solutions backlog increased to $25 million (enterprise, contractors, data center operators and AI infrastructure players, with strategic MSA contracts); Duos' 2026 goal remains approximately 25 megawatts ('we are 100% on plan') and it now has more than 75 megawatts under contract following the Axe Compute expansion; its local funnel is 'well over 100 megawatts in 5 to 10 meg tranches' for this year, from Tier 1 credit customers, with no one customer taking up all its bandwidth.
quarterly_data.figure: Technology Solutions backlog $25 million; more than 75 megawatts under contract; approximately 25 megawatts in 2026; funnel well over 100 megawatts

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker / CFO Adrian Goldfarb on the Columbus, Georgia GPU program: Duos bought the Columbus building at the beginning of July and installed over 7 megawatts of new infrastructure - generators, cooling plant, cabinets, lighting and 17,000 square foot of raised floor - in under 60 days; Columbus is being equipped to support 2,304 NVIDIA B300 GPUs. 'The HydraHost deployment remains one of the most significant opportunities in the company's history', with customer deposits already received and additional funding milestones under the contract; GPU revenue of $4.4 million per month 'will start here very soon'. Duos holds $18.8 million of long-term deferred revenue including the customer prepayment under its GPU program, and paid $68.8 million of deposits against its GPU equipment program and $5.8 million of deposits on real estate and edge data construction.
quarterly_data.figure: 2,304 NVIDIA B300 GPUs; over 7 megawatts installed in under 60 days; $4.4 million per month GPU revenue; $68.8 million GPU equipment deposits; $18.8 million long-term deferred revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker: the Nistar deal represents approximately 2 megawatt of contracted capacity supporting high-density AI compute, with deployment activities progressing in line with the planned mutual deployment schedule; it is expected to contribute recurring colocation revenue as capacity comes online and utilization ramps.

CEO Doug Recker: Duos announced an opportunity with Zero Latency company 0LAT covering up to 15 sites and 225 cabinets - a nonbinding term sheet with a bare metal provider that is looking at all 15 of Duos' sites, 'It's a 10-year deal'.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 15 sites and 225 cabinets; 10-year deal (nonbinding term sheet)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker on the market: Duos' niche is 1 to 20 meg in Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets with stranded power priced around $0.04 to $0.07 a kilowatt hour, plus powered sites of unsuccessful bit miners in the 5 to 20 megawatt range, within 130 miles and under five milliseconds; it has deployed modular for the last nine years and holds a patent on a clean room for GPUs; pods and facilities last well over 20 years (UPS batteries swapped over 10 to 12 years). Enterprise customers moving from 15 kW or 20 kW cabinets to 60 kW cannot be served by landlocked legacy data centers, Fortune 100s are asking to deploy a meg or two, and 'if I had 4 megawatt right now available today, I have probably 16 customers lined up to take it'.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 to 20 meg niche; $0.04 to $0.07 a kilowatt hour; probably 16 customers for 4 megawatt available today; pods well over 20 years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Doug Recker / CFO Adrian Goldfarb: Duos completed the sale of its rail business, Duos Technologies, Inc., on August 5 - it is now an independent privately held company under the Duos TI brand, Duos provides certain transition services, and rail is reported as discontinued operations - completing the transition to a pure-play AI infrastructure and edge data center company. The New APR Energy asset management agreement was amended beginning in the first quarter to reduce the scope of services, with revenues winding down through the third quarter. Duos ended Q2 with $112.3 million of cash, is effectively debt-free, and generated positive operating cash flow of $11.9 million from continuing operations in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: cash $112.3 million; first-half operating cash flow $11.9 million

contracts.signal: CEO Doug Recker: Duos signed 'a five-year colocation agreement with Axe Compute, Inc., a neocloud AI infrastructure platform to provide 10 megawatts of critical IT load capacity at our Columbus, Georgia campus', valued at more than $111 million in contracted revenue over the initial term and expected operational during the fourth quarter of 2026 (straight colo, unlike the first Columbus deployment that involves GPUs). New service orders announced the same day add up to 55 megawatts gross, in addition to the 10 meg, across multiple U.S. locations under a five-year agreement - an expected $500 million plus in aggregate base payments over the initial term. A related agreement contemplates cash equity investments by Axe Compute of up to $140 million in the project (subject to approvals, financing, final technical design and other conditions), the new data centers to be owned 51% by Duos and 49% by Axe Compute through an SPV that Duos manages, with Axe as lessee and offtaker (COO Dipan Patel). Initial readiness is targeted from late 2026 into early 2027, the second piece by the end of the first quarter; sites in Texas, South Carolina, Iowa and Alabama (a few in LOI status) already have utility power; Duos is coming in under 6 million a megawatt and contributes basically 30 million per site. Asked about the end customer of the Axe deal, the CEO said 'they are a Tier 1 hyperscaler' (not disclosed), on a five-year term.
contracts.units: 10 MW (Columbus, Georgia) plus up to 55 MW gross across multiple U.S. locations
contracts.value: more than $111 million (10 MW); $500 million plus aggregate base payments (55 MW); Axe Compute equity up to $140 million
contracts.date_signed: 10 MW agreement after the prior call; 55 MW service orders announced 08-17-2026
